## **What Is AI Lip Sync?**


AI lip sync makes a person in a video appear to speak or sing along to completely new audio.


The AI analyzes facial movements, especially around the mouth, and adjusts them so they match the uploaded sound.


Lip sync can replace dialogue or synchronize a visible performance to another audio track. For translation, approve the translated meaning and pronunciation before generating the synchronized video.


## **Lip Sync vs Talking Photo: What Is the Difference?**


Lip sync works with an existing video where a person is already moving and speaking on screen. A talking photo tool starts with a still image and animates it so the subject appears to talk or sing. If you already have a video, use lip sync. If you only have a photo, use Talking Photo instead.


Use the input you actually have. Rebuilding an existing performance from a still image can discard the original head movement and camera motion.


If you have a still photo instead of a video,[Magic Hour's Talking Photo](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-talking-photo) tool is what you need.


## **What You Need Before You Start**


Before creating your first lip synced video, gather the following:


- A short MP4 or MOV video with one clearly visible face
- A clear audio recording of the line or song, with similar duration
- Permission to use the video, voice, and likeness for your project
- A browser; no account is required for the guest trial


The free video trial is limited to ten seconds. Start with a representative sample before choosing a longer account-based job.


## **How to Lip Sync a Video With AI: Step by Step**


### **Step 1: Go to Magic Hour's Lip Sync Tool**


Open[Magic Hour's Lip Sync tool](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) in your browser. The tool loads directly from the web, so there is nothing to install.


### **Step 2: Upload Your Video**


Click the upload button and choose the video you want to modify. Videos where the subject is clearly facing the camera generally produce the most natural-looking results.


### **Step 3: Upload Your Audio**


Upload the approved audio track. For a first trial, record “Pick the blue box. Pause. Now press play.” Include the pause in the recording and keep the line within ten seconds. This gives you a concrete moment to inspect for unwanted mouth movement during silence.


### **Step 4: Click Generate**


Select the generation button shown in the tool and allow the job to finish. Keep the page or saved project available so you can return to the result. Processing time varies with the input, settings, and queue.


### **Step 5: Review and Download**


Watch the complete output with sound, then inspect pauses, head turns, teeth, and face edges. Download the sample and confirm its duration, crop, and watermark before generating a longer version.


## Use the full editor for mode and timing controls


After the guest trial, open the[signed-in Lip Sync editor](https://magichour.ai/create/lip-sync) . Select Add Video and Add Audio, check both trim selections, then choose Lip Sync Mode. The free route accepts uploaded or preset media; the full editor also supports YouTube video and voice-generation options.


Lite suits a simple first sample. Standard and Pro require visible mouth movement in the source; Pro requires Creator or higher. A still portrait belongs in Talking Photo. If you use Voice Cloner, finish generating the speech first: choosing a voice reference alone does not supply the final audio.


The selected video cannot exceed the available audio, and the result uses the shorter selected segment. For an illustrative 20-second source with 12 seconds of approved speech, select a matching video section before submitting. Check where each selection starts if the words arrive late. Lip Sync changes mouth movement; it does not retime the entire performance or change audio tempo. Review the estimate, select Generate Video and inspect the completed result. See the[mode, duration and troubleshooting guide](https://help.magichour.ai/en/articles/15011107-lip-sync-free-tool-vs-create-modes-limits-timing-and-troubleshooting) .


## **Tips for the Best Results**


- Keep the face unobstructed and in frame.
- Use a clear recording with one speaker for the first attempt.
- Check audio and video start times if the entire track is consistently early or late.
- Keep intentional pauses; remove unwanted leading silence only when it causes a timing mismatch.
- Change the input or setting related to a visible failure before spending another attempt.


## **Common Mistakes New Lip Sync Users Make**


- Using low-resolution videos. Blurry footage gives the AI less facial detail to work with, which can reduce lip sync accuracy.
- Uploading videos where the person's face is partially hidden. Sunglasses, hands, microphones, or objects covering the mouth can make synchronization less reliable.
- Choosing clips with heavy motion blur or fast camera movement. Stable footage usually produces better results.
- Using audio with loud background noise. Clear speech or vocals help the AI match mouth movements more accurately.
- Expecting AI to fix poor source material. Even the best lip sync tools perform better when both the video and audio are clean.


## **What Can You Use AI Lip Sync For?**


- Dubbing videos into different languages while matching mouth movements.
- Making a person appear to sing along to a song.
- Creating funny social media clips and meme videos.
- Syncing voiceovers to silent footage.
- Producing content without needing to reshoot video.


For an explainer or product video, check the surrounding edit too. A corrected voice line does not update an outdated caption, label, or screen recording.
